page.content:
Justinian's great church and the empire's architectural emblem.

How Hagia Sophia connects

  • Location: Constantinople — Hagia Sophia stands in Constantinople.
  • Character: Justinian I — Justinian rebuilt Hagia Sophia after the Nika riots.
  • Faction: Eastern Orthodox Church — Hagia Sophia was the patriarchal cathedral.
  • Topic: Byzantine Empire — Hagia Sophia is the empire's emblematic church.
  • Event: Nika riots — The riots destroyed the earlier Hagia Sophia Justinian then rebuilt.

What is Hagia Sophia?

Hagia Sophia was rebuilt by Justinian I after the Nika riots as the patriarchal cathedral of Constantinople — a dome of imperial Orthodoxy later converted to a mosque after 1453.

Key threads lead to Constantinople, Justinian I, Eastern Orthodox Church, Byzantine Empire and Nika riots.
